newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Ryanair seen launched at 195 Irish pence.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Ryanair seen launched at 195 Irish pence.

text.p: Ireland's low-cost airline Ryanair Holdings Plc is expected to command a launch price of 195 Irish pence per share when it floats on the market on Thursday afternoon, analysts believe.

Ryanair, which makes its debut on both New York's Nasdaq and Ireland's ISEQ index, the first Irish company to seek a simultaneous quote both sides of the Atlantic, will announce an initial public offering of 54.2 million ordinary shares with an additional over-allotment of 6.0 million shares.

Analysts had been forecasting a range of 180-190 Irish pence for the shares but strong demand for the stock, which is believed to be 15 times oversubscribed, has pushed the launch price up to 195 pence, analysts said.
"We believe there is strong demand out of New York and on this side of the Atlantic," one dealer said.
A 50/50 split in take-up of stock between the United States and Ireland/Europe is anticipated.
"The U.S. is expected to take about half the issue and the rest is split fairly equally between Ireland, 25 percent and Europe 25 percent," one dealer said.
Ryanair shares are expected to start trading in Dublin next week but investors will be able to trade on the "grey" Nasdaq market in New York in advance of the completion of the full listing.

Ryanair, which has been operating for 12 years and has a fleet of 13 Boeing 737-200 aircraft, with a future delivery of six new aircraft expected by November, said the funds will be used to cut debt, which is now 35 million Irish pounds ($52.8 million).
It will also allow the airline to be in a position to buy aircraft when necessary, it said when it announced its intention to float on May 6.
Speculation the company would seek a listing mounted after U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman became Ryanair chairman in December 1996 after taking a 20 percent stake in the airline.

Bonderman took over from former GPA chief Tony Ryan whose family founded Ryanair. After the offer, the Ryan family will own 35.3 percent of the company, down from 61.7 percent, while Irish Air and chief executive Michael O'Leary will own 15.7 and 14.1 percent, respectively.
The flotation will comprise an offer of shares to investors in Ireland, a public offer in the U.S. and offers to professional investors in the UK and Continental Europe, Ryanair said.
Ryanair said in its statement on May 6 that its strategy was to aim for 20 to 30 percent sales growth a year and increase flights on existing routes.
Morgan Stanley & Co International Ltd have been appointed global co-ordinator and bookrunner for the issue.

The offer will be underwritten by Morgan Stanley, Investment Bank of Ireland, CS First Boston and the Robinson Humphrey Company, Inc. Morgan Stanley and IBI Corporate Finance will act as joint sponsors and financial advisers to Ryanair and Davy Stockbrokers will be brokers to the issue.reuter csl/ajh
